text_blocks.snippet: Post-COVID, some individuals experience a range of heart issues, including arrhythmia, blood clots, myocarditis, pericarditis, and heart failure. These conditions can arise due to inflammation caused by the virus, potentially affecting the heart's electrical signals, muscle, or the lining of blood vessels. A study by Mount Sinai found that some patients with persistent cardiopulmonary symptoms after COVID-19 experienced long-term changes in their heart, including the development of cardiac and pulmonary diseases.

list.snippet: COVID-19 can disrupt the heart's electrical signals, leading to irregular heartbeats (Cleveland Clinic).

list.title: Blood Clots:
list.snippet: Inflammation can affect blood vessel linings, increasing the risk of blood clots, which can cause heart attacks or strokes.

list.title: Myocarditis:
list.snippet: This inflammation of the heart muscle is a potential complication of COVID-19.

list.title: Pericarditis:
list.snippet: Inflammation of the membrane surrounding the heart can cause chest pain and fluid buildup.

list.title: Heart Failure:
list.snippet: Excess fluid and swelling (edema) can develop in the lungs and body due to heart issues.
